title: OpenBSD 8.0
summary: OpenBSD 8.0 was a major release of the renowned open-source BSD operating system, continuing its tradition of security-first design, code correctness, and comprehensive documentation. This release included updates to the kernel, system utilities, and various security enhancements typical of OpenBSD's conservative development approach.
problem_solved: Provides a free, open-source operating system with industry-leading security defaults and code correctness, suitable for servers, workstations, and security-focused deployments.
why_valuable: OpenBSD consistently contributes security innovations (like OpenSSH, pledge, and unveil) back to the open-source community while maintaining a strict open documentation policy, making it invaluable for security-critical applications.
